issues.failure_explanation: The abstract asserts existence and uniqueness under only invertible-M-matrix and nonnegative-right-hand-side assumptions. For scalar A=2 and b=1/2, both x=1−1/sqrt(2) and x=1+1/sqrt(2) are nonnegative solutions, even within the paper's coefficient assumptions. For A=2 and b=2, no nonnegative solution exists because 2x−x²≤1 for x≥0. The theorem establishes only a unique small-norm branch under additional coefficient and smallness conditions.

failure_location.quote: Existence and uniqueness of a nonnegative solution is proved.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the abstract and introductory guarantees to the normalized matrix class, the stated bound on b, and uniqueness within the small-norm region.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised general existence and uniqueness guarantee is false; the restricted small-solution theorem does not justify it.
issues.title: Unqualified nonnegative existence and uniqueness exceeds the proved scope
issues.why_classification: The supported repair excludes the advertised general-M-matrix regime and replaces unrestricted nonnegative uniqueness by uniqueness of a selected branch.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there is  a unique $G=T(g)+E_G+\one v_G^T\in \EQT_{\infty}$ such that $G\geq 0$, $\|G\|_{\infty}<1 $ and  $(I-G)^2=A$;

issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions on A do not force an arbitrary square root G to be the distinguished branch from Lemma lem:square. Take A=I and G=−I=I−T(2), with all correction vectors and matrices zero. The stated assumptions on A and G²=A hold, but ||g||_W=2 contradicts the first conclusion. The proof imports the small-norm property of the distinguished complement without identifying G with that branch.

issues.failure_explanation: A solution of (A−||x||_1 I)x=b need not make the shifted matrix invertible. For example, let a(z)=(z²+z⁻²)/10, A=(9/5)I_3−T_3(a), b=(0,1/100,0)^T, and x=(4/5,1/10,4/5)^T. These data satisfy the paper's coefficient bounds, x is a nonnegative solution, and ||x||_1=17/10 is an eigenvalue of A. Thus the inverse used in the forward proof is undefined. The later invertibility argument applies only on the small-norm interval.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We consider a general $M$-matrix $A$, where $A=(2-\|M\|_{1})I - M$ with $M\geq 0$ and $\|M\|_1<1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The generalization requires ||b||_1<(1−||M||_1)², whereas the construction controls b using ||M||_∞; these norms have no ordering that supplies the required bound. For example, M has both rows (0.4,0.05), so ||M||_1=0.8 and ||M||_∞=0.45. With σ=0.05 and equal raw entries of b, the construction gives b=(1/8,1/8)^T and ||b||_1=0.25>0.04. These admissible construction inputs actually have no nonnegative solution: any such solution must have equal components and satisfy μ(0.75−μ)=0.25, whose left-hand side is at most 0.140625.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use (1−||M||_1−σ)² for the right-hand-side norm and require 0<σ<1−||M||_1; regenerate or verify the affected experimental data.
issues.overall_effect: The test-data generator does not ensure the hypotheses of the existence and convergence results and can generate problems with no required solution.
issues.title: The random right-hand-side construction uses the wrong matrix norm
issues.why_classification: A contained construction repair restores the theory, but it changes the generated problems and requires renewed validation of the reported experiments.
